item.title: Rain gardens offer a balanced solution for managing urban stormwater near Tokyo
item.description: Urban flooding is becoming a growing concern in densely developed neighborhoods, where paved surfaces limit infiltration and intense rainfall can overwhelm drainage systems. Low impact development measures, such as rain barrels (RBs) and rain gardens (RGs), help manage stormwater close to where it falls. RBs collect rooftop runoff for later nonpotable use, while RGs use vegetated depressions and soil to encourage infiltration. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Greenwashing fears may drive up the cost of climate finance
item.description: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions from industries such as steelmaking, chemicals and energy production requires enormous investment. item.title: Arctic ice had been expanding for 1,000 years before reaching its greatest extent around 1960
item.description: A recent study indicates that the Barnes Ice Cap had begun expanding nearly 2,000 years ago. This expansion was attributed to cooler summer conditions that allowed ice to grow. However, rising greenhouse gas emissions reversed this trend and caused significant ice retreat since the 1960s. Researchers emphasize that human-induced warming has disrupted natural climate patterns that favored renewed glacial growth. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: As flood risk rises, some communities question the idea of resilience
item.description: Climate change is increasing flood risk across the U.K. As floods become more frequent and intense, communities are increasingly encouraged to become resilient and "live with water." Yet in some flood-prone areas, residents are rejecting these calls, concerned that resilience is less about helping communities and more about transferring responsibility from institutions to citizens.
